SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MAY 28, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
PUBLIC ADVISORY: THIS MEETING WILL BE CONDUCTED IN A HYBRID MODEL WITH BOTH IN-PERSON ATTENDANCE AND VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda packet is available at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st Floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours as posted. Materials received after posting of the agenda will also be available for public inspection. For assistance, contact the Office of the City Clerk at city_clerk@cerritos.gov or (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council may reorder agenda items by majority vote of members present.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public may observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov/agendas or the City’s YouTube channel , on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public comment may be provided in person, remotely via Zoom, or in writing as described below. Public comment on business agenda items will be heard during consideration of that business item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be heard during Agenda Item No. 6.
Remote/teleconference (Zoom) participation :
PLEASE ENSURE YOUR ZOOM SOFTWARE IS UPDATED TO PROVIDE LIVE COMMENTS
Meeting ID: 897 8691 1692
Smart Phone or Computer (Zoom App required): https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89786911692
Phone Call-In: (669) 900-6833
To request to speak via Zoom, join or call in at the meeting start time and use the “Raise Hand” feature or press *9 by phone during the item on which you wish to speak. Press *6 to unmute when prompted.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Written comments may be submitted by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or delivered to the Office of the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. Timely comments will be distributed to the legislative body and retained as part of the official record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.

City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
MAY 28, 2026, 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA AND VIA ZOOM TELECONFERENCE,
MEETING ID# 897 8691 1692.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Rory Corrigan, Church in Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Women’s Club of Artesia-Cerritos.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama (arrived at approximately 8:21 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Lynda P. Johnson

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were announced by the City Council honoring:

  Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander Heritage Month; and

  Jewish-American Heritage Month.

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by majority action, reordered the agenda as follows:

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to reorder the agenda
  to consider Item 5B following consideration of New and Old Business Item 9B.

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory
  Boards (Commissions and Committees) (2025-2027 Term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 28, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 2 of 10

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding Advisory Board appointment
  procedures and suggested the establishment of additional eligibility criteria for
  service on the City’s Commissions and Committees.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  No action was taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Robert Shavelle expressed support for potential changes to the City’s administration
  and management of the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course.

  David Pylman spoke regarding City Council meeting management procedures and
  expressed concern regarding recent changes to public meeting facilitation.

  Kurtis Forsythe expressed concern regarding State and County public health and
  vaccination policies during the COVID-19 pandemic and submitted documents for the
  official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are
  considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk.)

  Kirit Chauhan expressed support for the continued funding of City-sponsored
  community events, community services, and public safety programs.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council
  received five (5) written comments submitted for Item 6 for inclusion in the official
  record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can
  be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, May 11, 2026, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular
  Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Monday,
  May 11, 2026, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 28, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 10

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated May 28, 2026 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  May 28, 2026  $9,129,969.96 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending March
  31, 2026 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Pulido, to approve City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending March 31,
  2026 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Notify and direct commencement of the 2026 Conflict of Interest Codes biennial
  review pursuant to requirements of the California Political Reform Act (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Pulido, to notify and direct the
  City Clerk to commence the 2026 biennial review of the City, Successor Agency, and
  Public Financing Authority Conflict of Interest Codes in compliance with the
  requirements of the California Political Reform Act (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 28, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 4 of 10

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A PROJECT LIST TO BE FUNDED BY SENATE BILL
  1: ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT FUNDS, FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-
  2027 (COUNCIL).

  Agenda Item 7D was pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration by
  Councilmember Hong, who then recused herself from the vote on this item, citing a
  potential conflict of interest due to her residence within 500 feet of the subject
  project area. She left her seat at the dais and left the room for the consideration of
  this item.

  City Manager Robert A. Lopez also recused himself from the consideration of this
  item, citing a potential conflict of interest due to his residence within 500 feet of the
  subject project area. He left the room for the consideration of this item.

  There was no discussion or deliberation on this item and no public comments were
  received.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2026-14, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING A PROJECT LIST TO BE FUNDED BY
  SENATE BILL 1: ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT FUNDS, FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 0 – 2 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Hong (recused), Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

  At the conclusion of the vote on the above-referenced item, Councilmember Hong
  and City Manager Robert A. Lopez returned to the meeting. Councilmember Hong
  resumed her seat at the dais.

7E.  Standing Agenda Item: Potential consideration of the Swim and Fitness Center
  Rehabilitation Project, Project No. 20201 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Hong, and seconded by Pulido, to take no action at this
  time and defer consideration of the Swim and Fitness Center boiler replacement
  until such time that the existing boiler system requires replacement (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 5 of 10

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of an appeal of a decision of the Cerritos Property
  Preservation Commission finding that Property Preservation Commission Case No.
  PPC 2026-13 located at 19435 Ellen Way, Cerritos, constitutes a property
  nuisance as set forth in Chapter 6.20 of the Cerritos Municipal Code and setting
  forth a ten (10) day abatement period thereon in Resolution No. P.P.C. 2026-10
  (COUNCIL).

  Mayor Johnson requested the City Council confirm if any Councilmembers conducted
  any ex-parte communications or conversations, or made any public statements to
  the press or on social media regarding a position on this administrative appeal.

  All City Councilmembers confirmed they did not conduct any ex-parte
  communications.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing.

  Joseph Chacon, Code Enforcement Manager, provided testimony.

  Rudy Hernandez, appellant, provided testimony.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Celia Spitzer spoke in support of enforcement of Cerritos Municipal Code regulations.

  David Pylman spoke in support of upholding the Property Preservation Commission’s
  decision.

  Noting no other individuals elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared
  the public hearing and the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2026-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL UPHOLDING A DECISION OF THE PROPERTY PRESERVATION
  COMMISSION (PROPERTY PRESERVATION COMMISSION RESOLUTION
  NO. P.P.C. 2026-10) FINDING THAT CASE NO. PPC 2026-13 LOCATED AT
  19435 ELLEN WAY, CERRITOS, CONSTITUTES A PROPERTY NUISANCE AS
  SET FORTH IN CHAPTER 6.20 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE AND
  SETTING FORTH A TEN (10) DAY ABATEMENT PERIOD THEREON IN
  RESOLUTION NO. P.P.C. 2026-10 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

8B.  (continued)

8B.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 5-0, to
  approve the following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2026-1, A
  REQUEST BY SIAM WELLNESS AND SPA TO PERMIT A MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENT
  USE WITH STATE-CERTIFIED MASSAGE THERAPISTS AT 20110 PIONEER

  IS ZONED AREA DEVELOPMENT PLAN EIGHTEEN (ADP-18) (APN 7055-017-023)*
  (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Amanda Acuna, Current Planning Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period. Noting no

  and the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hong, to waive full reading of
  and adopt Resolution No. 2026-16, A RESOLUTION OF THE CERRITOS CITY
  COUNCIL APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2026-1, A REQUEST BY
  SIAM WELLNESS AND SPA TO PERMIT A MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENT USE
  WITH STATE-CERTIFIED MASSAGE THERAPISTS AT 20110 PIONEER
  BOULEVARD, SUITE D, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT
  PROPERTY IS ZONED AREA DEVELOPMENT PLAN EIGHTEEN (ADP-18) (APN
  7055-017-023) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

8C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING THE 2025 URBAN
  WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN AND WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN
  PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA WATER CODE SECTIONS 10610 THROUGH 10657
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Chris Kuebert, Acting Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Kirit Chauhan requested clarification regarding any potential impacts of recent water
  and sewer rate adjustments to the Urban Water Management Plan and regarding
  infrastructure costs.

  Noting no other individuals elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared
  the public hearing and the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 28, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 7 of 10

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8C.  (continued)

  MOTION (DIED DUE TO LACK OF A SECOND): The motion concerning
  adoption of the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan (UWMP) and increased
  billing rates for water consumption levels over 30 units under Water Supply
  Shortage Level 3, within the UWMP, made by Tse, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2026-17, A RESOLUTION

  2025 URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN AND WATER SHORTAGE

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Johnson, to waive full reading

  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS ADOPTING THE 2025 URBAN WATER
  MANAGEMENT PLAN AND WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of authorization to relocate the City’s mobile Automated
  License Plate Reader trailer to various locations Citywide on an as-needed basis
  (COUNCIL).

  A report was given by Ryan Carey, Deputy City Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting, the City Council
  received full-text, unredacted copies of the five (5) written comments submitted for
  Item 9A, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record.
  Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made
  during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 28, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 8 of 10

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to include in the proposed
  Fiscal Year 2026-27 Combined Financial Program (City Budget), for City Council

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to authorize staff to

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to provide a report to the City

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, provided the following report from the Monday, May 11,

  The City Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A, 12B, and 12C
  as listed on the May 11, 2026 meeting agenda:

  12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Robert A. Lopez, City Manager; Pam Lee, City Attorney;
  Drew Schneider, Director of Administrative Services; Amy Thomas, Human
  Resources Manager; Lauren Vargas, Enterprise Services Manager
